title: Deadlock in money transfers
root_cause: transfer() locked rows in request order (sender FOR UPDATE then receiver FOR UPDATE). Concurrent opposite transfers A->B and B->A each hold one row lock and wait on the other, forming a wait cycle that Postgres aborts as 'deadlock detected', failing payments.
fix: Lock accounts in a consistent global order (sorted by id, min first) instead of request order, so concurrent opposite transfers no longer form a lock-wait cycle. Single-account (self) transfer handled with one SELECT FOR UPDATE. Semantics, return values and exceptions unchanged.

repro_report.example_violation: deadlock: opposite transfers 1<->2 failed with deadlock detected (5 deadlocks in batch 0)
